correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple unicyclic graph, weighted matrix-tree enumeration factors into a product over all bridge weights and an elementary cycle-deletion polynomial. The grounded Laplacian is an injective linear map in its independent edge weights, so logdet is strictly concave on its positive-definite domain and feasible KKT conditions are globally sufficient and unique. Euler homogeneity fixes \(\lambda=(N-1)/B\); bridge costs are spent equally. The omitted-edge derivative is sum reciprocal other cycle weights, giving the exact necessary-and-sufficient edge-deletion price inequality. For an entirely positive cycle, exclusion probabilities \(x_i\) satisfy \(x_i(1-x_i)=t c_i\) and \(\sum_i x_i=1\); elementary monotonicity proves exactly one of the two explicit root branches exists. The constructed solutions satisfy the KKT equations, the budget and support positivity. Four exact rational grounded determinant calculations, 168 numerical test graphs, and 6720 feasible competitor tests confirm implementation and examples; all-parameter proof is analytic and does not treat finite tests as exhaustive.

originality.rationale: Earlier literature supplies the graph-Laplacian D-optimality objective, the matrix-tree theorem, general logdet optimization, and unit-weight unicyclic topology classification, but the inspected statements do not imply the complete unique arbitrary heterogeneous edge-price conductance allocation on every fixed unicyclic graph. In particular, the precise \(c_j\ge\sum_{i\ne j}c_i\) deletion frontier, its irrelevance to attached tree topology and bridge prices, the global bridge-spend law and the constructive one-root formula are a strictly larger parameterized theorem than an equal-price cycle example. Searches for heterogeneous cost aliases, price-varying circuits, weighted spanning tree maximum and graph D-optimality found no direct coverage; non-retrieval is not proof of novelty. Risks remain from specialized classical optimal-design literature, finite scope of published-record search, and one general numerical-design paper inspected only in abstract.
residual_risks: The consulted literature does not exhaust all historical experimental-design and graph electrical-network work; absence of a retrieved equivalent theorem is not proof of novelty.
The full text of the Sagnol–Harman general numerical D-optimality paper was not inspected, so an equivalent worked example cannot be ruled out.
The previously treated equal-price cyclic restricted case is not itself new; only the heterogeneous-price complete classification is the assessed contribution.

value.rationale: A fixed arbitrary unicyclic graph with independently priced conductances is a natural rank \(N-1\) D-optimal information-design instance with N variables, broad tree attachments and a real k-dimensional positive cost vector. The theorem gives a globally unique complete classification via one monotone scalar root, exact allocation on all bridges, and sharp dominant-cost edge deletion that can change the optimal support. The exact edge-deletion threshold and independence of all attached-tree geometry provide motivated structural information beyond routine normalization or a computational sample. It offers a reproducible exact benchmark for budgeted graph sensing and logdet Laplacian optimization.
